title: [MEGATHREAD] October 2026 Cybersecurity Incidents: PHP2Shell, LiteLLM, eMudhra, GitLab, and more
description: In October 2026, critical remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) were discovered in PHP affecting multiple supported versions. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely due to out-of-memory corruption and stale global state issues. Emergency security updates were released on October 21, 2026, for PHP versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. Mitigations exist but are incomplete; updating to the fixed versions is strongly recommended. Additional incidents involving LiteLLM, eMudhra, GitLab, Railway, and Zeabur were also reported in the same timeframe. The PHP project continues to address these issues with further advisories and release candidates.

aiSummary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) allow unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory handling that can interrupt PHP while internal request data is partially initialized, leading to request cleanup treating invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state where request-owned internal state survives after memory is freed, allowing subsequent requests to use stale data before initialization. These affect PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, with the highest risk on mod_php. Emergency updates were released for PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. Partial mitigations include configuration changes like disabling session.upload_progress and adjusting memory limits, but only updating fully resolves the issue. The PHP project also provided minimal backports for older versions and is preparing a full advisory for a related issue (CVE-2026-115560). Other significant cybersecurity incidents in October 2026 include supply chain compromises in LiteLLM, certificate authority compromise at eMudhra, and critical vulnerabilities in GitLab, with official advisories and responses published by respective vendors and organizations.
aiImpact: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected PHP installations, potentially compromising web servers before any application code runs. The risk is highest for mod_php configurations, where exploitation has been demonstrated. This can lead to full server compromise, data theft, or further network intrusion. The vulnerabilities affect all PHP installations serving web requests across multiple PHP versions. Other related incidents in October 2026 include supply chain compromises and certificate authority breaches, which pose additional risks to trust and security in affected ecosystems.
